output_text: A 7-year-old British schoolgirl, India Mayhew, has died after being thrown from a horse while on holiday in India with her family. The incident occurred at a riding facility in Matheran, 20 miles east of Mumbai, when the horse suddenly bolted and dragged her a distance, causing serious head injuries. Her parents, who were also on the holiday, chose not to press charges against the operator, stating it was an accident. The police have registered a case of accidental death, and the British Deputy High Commission in Mumbai is providing consular assistance to the family.

Austrian designers Maya Pindeus and Johanna Pichlbauer have created a robot called the "Beautification machine" that applies makeup, specifically eyeliner and lipstick, to a person's face. The device consists of three components: a lipstick wheel, an eyeliner applicator, and a mask that illuminates when the process is complete. While the machine is intended to simplify the makeup application process, it appears to have some precision issues, as seen in a video of women testing the device. The machine's creators showcased their invention at the Biennale Internationale Design Saint-Etienne 2015 in France as part of their art project.

A former US Army enlistee, John T. Booker Jr., was arrested and charged with attempting to detonate a car bomb at Fort Riley military base in Kansas. Booker, who also used the alias Mohammed Abdullah Hassan, had previously posted on Facebook about the "adrenaline rush" of dying in jihad and had expressed plans to commit an insider attack against American soldiers. The "bomb" was actually a non-explosive device created by confidential informants, and no one was in danger. Booker had enlisted in the Army last year but was terminated after the FBI questioned him about his Facebook posts and he waived his Miranda rights, revealing his plans to commit an attack.

England's push for victory in the first Test against the West Indies was led by Gary Ballance, who scored his fourth Test century in just nine matches. However, the day's highlight belonged to Chris Jordan, who made a stunning catch to dismiss Darren Bravo, leaving West Indies at 98 for two and 340 runs short of their target. England's Alastair Cook set a challenging target of 438 for the West Indies, but they began their chase solidly, reaching 90 for one before Jordan's catch. England remains firm favorites to secure a valuable victory, but all results are still possible.

Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren expressed relief that Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has been found guilty of the Boston bombing, but does not support the death penalty. Warren believes Tsarnaev should spend his life in jail without the possibility of parole, stating that he should "die in prison." This stance aligns with her long-held anti-death penalty views. The case will now move to the penalty stage of the trial, where the jury will decide whether to sentence Tsarnaev to life in prison or the death penalty.

Tokyo's Narita Airport has installed brightly-colored running tracks in its new Terminal 3 to celebrate the 2020 Olympics. The cushioned tracks, which include directional information, serve as a useful navigation tool for passengers, with blue lanes leading to departures and red lanes to arrivals. The airport opted for the running tracks to save money, instead of installing traditional moving walkways or illuminated signs. The new terminal, primarily used for low-cost carrier departures, first opened on April 8.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce is interested in signing Leeds United midfielder Alex Mowatt, who has impressed this season with nine goals. Mowatt, a 20-year-old England U20 international, has drawn attention from several Premier League clubs and was scouted by Hull during a recent match against Wolves. Bruce is keen to bolster his squad with homegrown talent, and Mowatt is one of several promising Leeds players who could be targeted in the summer. Mowatt graduated from Leeds' academy in 2013 and has since become a key player for the first team.

Parma, a Serie A club, has been deducted four points by the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) for breaching financial regulations. This adds to the three points they were previously penalized, leaving them with a total of 12 points from 30 games. The club is currently at the bottom of Serie A and has been struggling financially, with players not being paid all season. Parma was also declared bankrupt last month.

Emily Grimson, a 25-year-old model from Shropshire, has built a lucrative career as a hand model, earning up to £100 an hour. Despite being one of Britain's most successful models, her face is rarely seen, as her hands are in high demand for product videos, TV advertisements, and magazine ads. To maintain her perfect hands, Emily moisturizes them up to ten times a day and follows a strict beauty routine. She has been modeling full-time since autumn and is signed with BMA Models.

Northern Ireland's tourism board is responding to comments made by actor Kit Harington, who joked that Belfast is "wonderful for two or three days" during an appearance on a US late-night chat show. Harington, who plays Jon Snow in Game of Thrones, has spent five years filming in Belfast, which is a principal location for the show. Despite his lighthearted jabs, Belfast has become a popular city break destination in the UK, thanks in part to the show's popularity. Tourism bosses have leveraged the show's success to attract visitors to the city.

Burnley manager Sean Dyche has encouraged striker Danny Ings to focus on enjoying his game, rather than putting too much pressure on himself to score. Ings has not found the net in seven appearances and Dyche believes that if he starts to play with a smile, his goals will follow. Despite struggling for goals, Burnley has collected five points from a tough run of eight games, including victories over Manchester City and draws with Chelsea and Tottenham. Dyche is confident that his forwards will come good again and help the team avoid relegation.

Misty Machinshok, 33, has been sentenced to 15 to 30 years in prison for convincing her husband to repeatedly rape their 15-year-old daughter in order to conceive another child. Machinshok, who is no longer fertile, coached the pair on the best positions to conceive and even held her daughter's hand during the initial rapes. Her husband, Gary Machinshok, 29, has also pleaded no contest to raping the child and will be sentenced separately. Both victims are now in foster care, and the case has been described as one of the most heinous crimes a prosecutor has dealt with in 14 years.

Freddie Roach, trainer of Manny Pacquiao, believes Floyd Mayweather does not deserve to be considered the best fighter of their generation. Roach rates super-middleweight star Andre Ward and middleweight sensation Gennady Golovkin above Mayweather due to his perceived lack of competition and "ducking" of opponents. Roach thinks Mayweather has picked and chosen his fights, which is a major factor in his assessment. He is confident that Pacquiao will spring a surprise in the upcoming welterweight showdown against Mayweather.

A 19-year-old apprentice electrician, Nathan Brown, died after being electrocuted while testing lights at a factory in Rochdale, Greater Manchester. He fell 12ft from a ladder onto the roof of a toilet block after apparently touching exposed electrical bars powering a crane. Nathan was working with his father, an experienced electrician, at the time of the incident, which occurred in September 2013. He died from his injuries after being airlifted to hospital.

Scientists at Stanford University have created super-strong robots inspired by geckos, which can carry over 100 times their own weight. The robots, weighing as little as 9 grams, can haul heavy loads up vertical walls, with one model, μTug, able to drag a weight 2000 times heavier. The robots' "feet" are covered in tiny rubber spikes that mimic geckos' small hairs, allowing them to create a weak bond with the surface and climb up walls. These robots have potential applications in emergencies, factories, and construction sites.

Jarret Stoll, a 32-year-old hockey player for the L.A. Kings, was arrested on a drug-possession charge at a Las Vegas resort on Friday. He was charged with possession of cocaine and ecstasy and released on $5,000 bail. The Kings organization has launched an internal investigation and is withholding further comment until more information is gathered. Stoll has been with the Kings since 2008 and is reportedly in a relationship with TV personality Erin Andrews.

A man named Steve Spowart helped rescue five horses from severe flooding in New South Wales, Australia, after the worst storm in a decade hit the area. Spowart, wearing a black wetsuit, paddled out on his surfboard to reach the stranded horses, navigating through deep and murky water. With the help of the horses' owner, Sonia Sharrock, and others, Spowart successfully led the horses to safety, despite facing challenges such as barbed wire and frightened animals. The rescue efforts were captured in heartwarming photos and videos.

Four former Blackwater Worldwide security contractors were sentenced for their roles in a 2007 mass shooting in Baghdad that killed 17 people. Nicholas Slatten was sentenced to life in prison for his first-degree murder conviction, while Paul Slough, Evan Liberty, and Dustin Heard each received 30-year sentences. The contractors were convicted of various manslaughter and firearms charges after a federal jury found them guilty in October. The shooting, which saw the contractors open fire on innocent civilians, was deemed unjustified by an FBI investigation.

A 19-year-old man, Moses Yitzchok Greenfeld, drowned in Hampstead Heath pond in north London after getting into difficulty while swimming with friends. Eyewitnesses claim that at least seven police officers stood on the bank and watched as the teenagers tried to save their friend, with some even diving into the water to search for him. The police officers did not enter the water, and it is believed that the victim may have had a cardiac arrest due to the shock of jumping into the cold water. His body was eventually discovered five feet below the surface nearly six hours after he was reported in trouble.

Mary Day, a 60-year-old woman from Dorset, was found guilty of claiming £16,500 in income support and disability allowance despite having £27,000 in her bank account. She used the money to fund luxury holidays to Goa, India, and was caught after an anonymous tip-off to benefits officers. Day pleaded guilty to five counts of dishonestly failing to notify the Department for Work and Pensions of a change in circumstances, and was sentenced to 12 weeks in prison suspended for 12 months. She was also ordered to pay £165 in costs and a victim surcharge.

Two friends, Elvis Kwiatkowski and Chas Quye, have been sentenced to life in prison for the murder of Neill Buchel, a 39-year-old married father of two. Buchel was subjected to extreme and degrading pranks, inspired by the TV show "Jackass," before being killed and dismembered, with his body disposed of in a lake. The men had become obsessed with the pranks and had been making Buchel endure them for months before his death. Buchel had been living with a group of friends who were also involved in the pranks, and one of them, Scott "Gary" Hunt, was sentenced to five years for conspiracy to pervert the course of justice.

Apple has been granted a patent for a facial recognition system that would allow users to unlock their devices with a selfie. The system would use the front-facing camera to scan a user's face when the device is moved into a certain position, and automatically unlock the device if the image matches one on file. This method is similar to Android's "Trusted face" feature, but Apple's system would track the movement of the phone to determine whether it is being used or placed flat on a table. The patent was filed in 2011 and has now been awarded, suggesting that Apple may be considering implementing this feature in future devices.

Former US President George W. Bush visited a wounded soldier at Walter Reed hospital in Washington, D.C. during his presidency, where he was confronted by a grieving mother who was beside herself with grief over her child's condition. According to Bush's former press secretary Dana Perino, the mother yelled at the president, asking why her child was in the hospital bed instead of his. Perino said Bush "just stood and took it," allowing the mother to express her anguish before addressing the incident on the helicopter ride back to the White House. The president reportedly said, "That mama sure was mad at me. And I don't blame her a bit," and was seen with a single tear on his face.

David Marshall, a 68-year-old sex offender, has been sentenced to a minimum of 20 years and six months in prison for the murder of 20-year-old Eni Mevish, a forensic science student at Staffordshire University. Marshall, who was on licence for sexually assaulting a 14-year-old girl, stabbed Mevish in the heart, lungs, and liver after becoming jealous of her other friendships. The two had met six months prior to the incident while Mevish was out jogging, and Marshall had been providing her with financial support. Marshall attacked Mevish at her home after becoming angry when she was watching a film with a friend.

The Duchess of Cambridge is nearing her due date, and preparations are underway at her Norfolk home, Anmer Hall, for the new arrival. The nursery has been given a Beatrix Potter theme, with fittings from luxury children's furniture store Dragons of Knightsbridge. In a move that has sparked speculation over the baby's sex, Kate Middleton had several pots of pink paint delivered to Anmer Hall from Annie Sloan, including colors such as Henrietta, Antoinette, and Emile. The new baby will spend its first few weeks at Anmer Hall and also have a nursery at Kensington Palace.

The New York Police Department (NYPD) has revised its training materials, which are now being reviewed by a federal judge. The revised materials emphasize the importance of not engaging in racial profiling, telling or tolerating ethnic or racial jokes, and imitating speech patterns of others. The changes are a result of a 2013 federal ruling that deemed the NYPD's "Stop, Question and Frisk" practice unconstitutional, which disproportionately targeted African-American and Hispanic individuals. The revised 140-page training manual aims to promote equal treatment and respect for all individuals.

Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew believes Manchester City can still win the Premier League title despite Chelsea being six points clear with a game in hand. Pardew points to past instances where City came from behind to win the title, including last season and in 2012 when Sergio Aguero scored an injury-time winner. He thinks the Premier League title race is never over until the end, and City's recent history proves that. Pardew's comments come ahead of Palace's match against City on Monday.

UK Prime Minister David Cameron responded to criticism from Church of England bishops over the morality of his government's austerity and welfare policies. In an Easter message, Cameron stated that his government had spent five years trying to "lift people up" by making work pay and encouraging responsibility. This came after the Church published a guide criticizing the Coalition's welfare policies, which include a £26,000-a-year cap on household benefits and tough sanctions for jobless benefits. The bishops had accused the government of portraying welfare claimants as "undeserving" and "dependent."

Former QPR manager Harry Redknapp has revealed that he resigned from the club in February due to more than just his knee problems, which he initially cited as the reason. Redknapp described the situation at QPR as "a bit of a soap opera" and claimed that there were people with their own agendas working against him. He also mentioned that constant speculation about his replacement, particularly Tim Sherwood, and the constant media attention wore him down. Redknapp believes he would have helped QPR avoid relegation if he had stayed.

Former footballer Dion Dublin made his presenting debut on the BBC's "Homes Under the Hammer" alongside regular hosts Martin Roberts and Lucy Alexander. Dublin joined the show to help a brother and sister-in-law, Mike and Lucia, renovate a three-bedroom semi-detached house in Dartford that they purchased at auction for £215,000. Dublin seemed to be in his element, offering suggestions and ideas for the renovation, including overhauling the 80s-style kitchen and creating a kitchen diner. The show follows house buyers from the auction room to the completion of their renovation projects, with local estate agents valuing the properties at the end to determine if the buyers have made a profit.

In the Champions League quarter-final first leg, Juventus took the lead against Monaco with a penalty scored by Arturo Vidal in the 57th minute. The penalty was awarded after Juventus forward Alvaro Morata was tripped by Monaco defender Ricardo Carvalho inside the box. The incident was a result of a 70-yard pass from Andrea Pirlo that caught Carvalho off guard, allowing Morata to make a run towards goal. The goal gave Juventus a crucial advantage in the tie, with the match ending 1-0 in their favor.

Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal has warned his players that Champions League qualification is not yet assured, despite holding an eight-point gap over Liverpool. Van Gaal sees next Sunday's derby against Manchester City as crucial in the battle to finish runners-up, and also as an opportunity to push for a top-two finish. He emphasized that complacency should not risk success, as United still have to play the other top-four teams. Van Gaal also hinted that Angel Di Maria may return to the starting lineup soon, but will wait for the right moment.

Eve Addison, a 24-year-old marketing manager, initially thought she had an allergy after developing a swelling in her collarbone after drinking gin and tonic. However, after switching brands and experiencing night sweats and a rash, she was diagnosed with Hodgkin Lymphoma, a type of cancer that affects the lymphatic system. The swelling in her collarbone was actually an enlarged lymph node, a common symptom of the condition. After undergoing six months of chemotherapy, Addison has been given the all-clear and is now sharing her story to raise awareness about the condition.

UK Education Secretary Nicky Morgan has stated that she would quit the Cabinet if the Conservative Party enters a power-sharing deal with Ukip. This comes after Ukip leader Nigel Farage sparked controversy with comments about people with HIV coming to Britain, which Morgan described as "stomach-turning" and "calculated" to appeal to Ukip's core vote. Morgan's comments suggest she would not be willing to serve in a coalition with Ukip, which has been a possibility if the Conservatives fail to secure a majority in the upcoming election.

A 30-year-old Philadelphia woman, Keonna Thomas, was arrested on Friday for attempting to join the Islamic State group and martyr herself. Authorities claim she communicated with an ISIS fighter in Syria, expressing her desire to participate in a martyrdom operation. Thomas had been under FBI surveillance for a week and had also expressed her extremist views on a now-deleted Twitter account. She will remain in custody until her next court appearance on April 8.

Jessica Carey surprised her grandmother, Patty Lawing, by revealing a tattoo of a younger version of herself on her forearm. The tattoo was based on a childhood portrait of Patty and was created by Jessica's husband, Aaron Carey. When Jessica showed the tattoo to her grandmother, Patty was overcome with emotion, shouting "oh my God" and shaking with excitement. The heartwarming moment was captured on camera and has only recently been shared online.

US aviation authorities have launched an investigation into a bizarre incident where a plane allegedly dumped toilet paper and plastic objects onto a neighborhood in West Pittston, Pennsylvania. Residents, including Paula Viccica, claim the debris came from a plane's lavatory holding tank, with some pieces landing in her well-kept front garden and trees. The FAA has stated that lavatory waste is typically contained in a holding tank until a plane lands, and it is "very rare" for anything to fall from an aircraft. The investigation aims to determine the cause of the incident and ensure the safety of the affected residents.

Nigel Farage, the leader of the UK Independence Party (Ukip), has been embroiled in controversy after far-right supporters, including a former English Defence League regional organiser named Gary Field, attended a Ukip event in South Thanet. Field, who has a criminal record for assault, was seen drinking beers and gesturing to onlookers while waiting for Farage's arrival. Farage initially denied any connection to the group, but they later posted a message on social media accusing him of wanting to distance himself from them. The incident has sparked a war of words between Farage and the group, with an anti-Ukip campaigner also reporting Field to police for alleged assault.

Rangers' top scorer Nicky Law has become a £500,000 target for several English Championship clubs, including Brighton, Birmingham, and Reading. Law has been in top form under interim manager Stuart McCall, scoring 12 goals this season, but his future at Rangers remains uncertain. The club is facing a summer of uncertainty with a dozen players out of contract, including midfielder Ian Black, who is attracting interest from Wigan. Law's representatives have received calls from ten English clubs, with final decisions yet to be made on his future.

Manchester City's chances of retaining the Barclays Premier League title were dealt a significant blow after a 2-1 loss to Crystal Palace. Glenn Murray scored a controversial goal in the first half, despite appearing to be offside, and Jason Puncheon added a second goal for Palace. Manchester City pulled one back through Yaya Toure, but the loss leaves them nine points adrift of leaders Chelsea and in fourth place. The defeat further loosens City's grip on the title, with Palace's win a significant upset.

Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin have finalized their divorce after a year of separation. The couple, who announced their "conscious uncoupling" in 2014, have reportedly signed the divorce documents and will file them on Monday. The divorce is said to be amicable, with the two using their business managers to work out a settlement agreement involving property and custody. The settlement is confidential, but insiders claim there were no major issues with money or custody of their two children.

A 5-year-old girl named Na Chu became trapped by her neck after falling between metal bars of a residential property in Xiangtan, south China. Neighbors rushed to her aid after hearing her terrified screams and managed to prop her up using a piece of pipe to prevent her from suffocating. Firefighters eventually arrived 30 minutes later to assist in the rescue. The heroic efforts of the neighbors have been widely praised on social media, with one neighbor being dubbed the "lifting man" for supporting the girl's legs during the rescue.

ISIS, despite its brutal reputation, has been operating a bureaucracy in areas under its control, issuing official documents such as birth certificates, vaccination schedules, and rent dispute notices. These documents, obtained by researcher Aymenn Al-Tamimi, provide a glimpse into the self-declared caliphate's attempt to establish stability and daily life. In Mosul, ISIS reopened the University of Mosul, but with a radically altered curriculum that banned subjects such as democracy, hotel management, and archaeology, which it considers to promote idol worship. The group's destruction of ancient artifacts and takeover of hotels also reflect its strict interpretation of Islamic law.

A company called UCO has released a new line of stormproof matches that can continue to burn even when submerged in water or buried underground. The matches have a tough coating that smolders and reignites when exposed to oxygen, making them ideal for survival situations. The UCO Stormproof Matches have undergone rigorous testing, including being submerged in water, buried in mud, and exposed to compressed air. The matches are available for £5.47 ($7.99) and come with 25 matches and three strike pads in a waterproof case.

A care home in Riverdale, New York, is conducting an experiment inspired by the 2004 film "50 First Dates" to help dementia patients. The experiment involves showing residents video recordings from loved ones each morning to ease confusion, forgetfulness, and agitation. The goal is to set a positive tone for the day without using medication, and to help residents recognize and connect with their loved ones. The program is designed for those in the early to moderate stages of dementia, and the care home plans to evaluate its effectiveness next month.

A 51-year-old mother, Lorraine Cobourn, was hit by a yellow taxi in Derby last year, suffering a broken hip and traumatic injuries. The incident has left her with a severe phobia of anything yellow, including bananas, yellow number plates, and yellow taxis. Cobourn has had to leave her job as a Barclays bank clerk and is undergoing counseling to cope with the psychological damage. She is trying to overcome her fear by exposing herself to yellow objects, including flowers, but the incident has had a significant impact on her life.

Zhao Pingan, known as China's 'miracle baby,' has celebrated his first birthday after being born prematurely when his mother was killed in a car crash in March. The baby's mother was in labor when she and her husband were hit by a truck while traveling on a motorbike to a hospital in Xiamen city, Fujian province. Pingan was given the name "safe and sound" in Chinese and was adopted by his uncle and grandmother after the accident. He celebrated his first birthday publicly in his hometown, surrounded by family and medical staff who treated him at the time.

Fabio Lovato, 30, proposed to his girlfriend Laura Knight, 29, in a unique and romantic way at their local Cineworld cinema in Gloucester. He created a one-minute and 30-second video showcasing pictures of their time together, including their meeting in Australia in 2013, which played after the trailers for Fast and Furious 7. The video ended with the words "Laura, I have a question for you," and Fabio then got down on one knee to pop the question. Laura was completely surprised and said yes, describing the moment as "absolutely amazing."

Cle 'Bone' Sloan, an alleged victim of Suge Knight, claims in a police interview that Knight growled "I'm going to kill you" before yanking on the gear stick, which was the moment before Knight allegedly killed Terry Carter and tried to kill Sloan by running over them in a Compton parking lot. Sloan describes the confrontation, stating that he and Knight exchanged blows before Knight made the threat. Sloan also claims that Knight appeared to be reaching for a gun on the passenger seat while moving the gear stick. The police interview was released after pictures emerged showing Knight with minimal facial injuries despite being punched multiple times during the confrontation.

The Havasupai tribe, the smallest Indian nation in America with over 600 members, resides in the depths of the Grand Canyon in Arizona. The tribe's village, Supai, is accessible only by hiking, helicopter, or mule, and is situated eight miles from the nearest road. The tribe relies on tourism, with around 20,000 visitors per year, as well as farming and weaving, but is vulnerable to flooding due to its location near Cataract Creek. The tribe has a unique way of life, with a cafe, general stores, a lodge, post office, school, and churches, and has a rich history, including a long-standing dispute over land ownership that was resolved in 1975.
